record.paper_title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory
record.original_question: How can one determine the minimal possible order of a representation for a given phase-type distribution? Here a phase-type distribution is the distribution of the absorption time in a finite-state absorbing Markov chain; a representation is the underlying Markov chain data, and its order is the number of transient states, equivalently the dimension of the generator matrix T. Given the Laplace transform f_tilde(s)=p(s)/q(s) of the probability density, with p and q coprime and deg q called the degree of the distribution, characterize or compute the smallest number of transient states among all phase-type representations of the same distribution.

evidence.quote: In particular the problem of finding the minimal order of a representation for a given PH distribution is still open.
The order of a representation is the number of transient states of the Markov chain which is the dimension of the matrix T.
The general problem of finding a minimal representation for a given PH-distribution is still open

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a non-negative random variable defined as the time to absorption of a continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space {1,2,...,n,n+1}, where states 1,...,n are transient and state n+1 is absorbing. Such a chain is determined by an initial probability row vector α ∈ R^n (with α_i ≥ 0 and α·1 ≤ 1) on the transient states and an n×n sub-generator matrix T with non-positive diagonal entries, non-negative off-diagonal entries, row sums ≤ 0, and T non-singular; the absorption vector is t = -T·1. The distribution of X (called a phase-type distribution with representation (α, T) of order n) has density f(x) = α e^{Tx} t for x ≥ 0, and Laplace transform f̃(s) = α(sI - T)^{-1} t, which can be written as a rational function p(s)/q(s) with p, q coprime polynomials; the integer deg q is called the algebraic degree of the distribution.

Problem: Given a phase-type distribution F (specified, e.g., by some representation (α, T) or by its Laplace transform f̃(s) = p(s)/q(s) with gcd(p,q) = 1), determine an algorithm — or a closed-form characterization in terms of (α, T) or of p and q — that computes the minimal order

  n*(F) := min { n : there exists a phase-type representation (α', T') of order n with α' e^{T'x}(-T'·1) = f(x) for all x ≥ 0 },

i.e., the smallest possible number of transient states among all phase-type representations of F.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding the minimal order (minimal number of transient states) of a phase-type representation for a given PH distribution is widely reported as still open in the general case. It is fully resolved for order 2, and a canonical (and minimal) representation has been obtained for order 3; for order ≥ 4 no symbolic/canonical procedure is known and the general minimality problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Order of Phase-Type Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Given a PH distribution, what is its order? ... the minimal number of states required to represent a given PH distribution as an absorbing CTMC.
status_evidence.claim: States the minimal-order problem and treats it as an open research question.

status_evidence.title: A Canonical Representation of Order 3 Phase Type Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: A canonical (minimal) representation of the PH(3) class is provided; no symbolical canonical transformation appears to exist for order 4 or higher.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is solved for order 3 but remains open for higher orders.

status_evidence.title: Phase-type distributions and representations (Commault & Mocanu)
status_evidence.snippet: The general problem of finding a minimal representation for a given PH-distribution is still open.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit statement that the general minimal representation problem is open.
